Guidance & outlook: Opex, I may not give a guidance because you know, this is a silent period , but I must say our o pex will be mostly focused on technology and human resources.

So that has already been done from the month of April itself and we are very confident that we will continue to do that because in majority of the cases the distribution channel is getting a percentage of the TER with increase or decrease as it happens in a dynamic manner.

The PMS, advisory and international is remaining 8%, but endeavo ur is to increase it further by increasing both sides. this number is as discussed earlier, though on the top line we are very high, but it's a low remunerative business majority, but we are getting into the high revenue AIF and PMS products going forward and that is the point.
Growth & demand: Turning to our industry, mutual fund QAAUM, that is quarterly average assets under management, grew around 15% year-on-year and remained broadly stable sequentially, driven by market strength and sustained retail flows.
SIP AUM increased by ₹2.1 trillion, reflecting 15% year-on-year growth and monthly SIPs grew by 14% to nearly ₹4,000 crores.
Operating profit stood at ₹907 crores, registering a healthy growth of 17% profit after tax, which stood at ₹873 crore s, registering 37% growth quarter-on-quarter basis.
Margins & costs: Gross margins across equity, debt, liquid, and passive strategies remained stable during the quarter, while net margins have improved at overall level despite change in regulation around transition to the base expense ratio and removal of exit load structu re.
We continue to manage these regulatory changes prudently to preserve long-term margin resilience.
But the history of 17% YoY growth in operating profit last quarter is what you can note down for today.
Capex & expansion: Equity -oriented assets saw a strong Y -o-Y expansion with notable outperformance in small and mid -cap segments during the quarter, whereas large-cap delivered more moderate gains.
Balance sheet & cash: Debt assets moderated due to institutional redemption patterns and tight short -term liquidity, while passive products continued to expand meaningfully as ETFs and index funds gained acceptance among both institutional and retail investors.
Yeah, on the dividend, I think we've been consistent last year we had paid a special dividend.
But that new dividend policy that we have created and put out there as public institution now, we will have a clear view of dividend.
Risks & challenges: The quarter has characterized by a steady domestic economic momentum, healthy corporate earnings, and constructive equity market conditions , even as global markets witnessed intermittent volatility in interest rates, liquidity, and commodities.

Slightly flattish because of the market volatility and geopolitical conditions, but we are maintaining that flow and the number of additions in last quarter 1.7 million is very, very huge number for us and gives a lot of strength to believe that SIP story is really coming up.
Despite volatility, our SIP AUM grown by 15% year -on-year and SIP flow also is 14%.
